status: independent semantic assertions derived from Sol's public field map; not compiler results
valid_case_rule: For each operation, all listed args have the declared typed value or reference, output type is retained, context preconditions hold, and undo equals required_undo. Reject when any negative assertion applies.

operations.positive: First action; followed by protected operations.
operations.negative: Not first, duplicated when policy allows only first, or malformed args.

operations.positive: Inside transaction after authorize; data is parent_input.
operations.negative: Outside transaction, wrong data input type, or missing delete_created.

operations.positive: Integer id from input or earlier visible step.
No arguments; output may be referenced later where visible.
operations.negative: Unexpected argument or unknown output field.

operations.positive: Inside transaction with integer id and parent_patch data.
operations.negative: Wrong id/data type, outside transaction, or missing restore_patch.

operations.positive: Inside transaction with integer parent id and child_input.
operations.negative: Wrong type, outside transaction, or missing delete_created.

operations.positive: Both ids are integer-typed and visible.
operations.negative: Either id has wrong type or is forward/cross-scope.

operations.positive: Integer parent id from a visible input/step.
operations.negative: Missing/wrong parent id or unknown output field.

operations.positive: Inside transaction with two integer ids and child_patch data.
operations.negative: Wrong type, outside transaction, or missing restore_patch.

operations.positive: Inside transaction; parent/children typed inputs and atomic batch contract applies.
operations.negative: Wrong input shape/type, outside transaction, or missing delete_created.

operations.positive: Integer parent id; workflow capability is one of the declared allowed workflow values.
operations.negative: Wrong/missing parent id, undeclared output, or capability mismatch.

operations.positive: csv workflow capability; integer parent id; string CSV; inside transaction; delete_created undo.
operations.negative: Without csv capability, wrong arg type, outside transaction, or missing undo.

operations.positive: Storage is s3 or gcs; operation is outside DB transaction; bytes do not flow to public result.
operations.negative: Storage none, inside DB transaction, wrong arg type, missing undo, or bytes result exposed.

operations.positive: Storage is s3 or gcs; outside DB transaction; returned object metadata may be used but body bytes are not exposed.
operations.negative: Storage none, inside DB transaction, wrong key type, or public bytes result.

assertions: Both explicit values are accepted where v6/v7 requires capabilities.
Missing, null, or unknown values are rejected.
Use no capabilities. cannot stand in for required v6/v7 fields.
Each declared provider is preserved in output semantics.
Unknown or omitted provider is rejected when the version requires it.
Authorization action must be first regardless of provider.
none forbids object.put/get.
s3 and gcs allow object.put/get subject to argument, transaction, undo, and result rules.
No implicit provider fallback is allowed.
workflow.import requires csv.
workflow.run requires a workflow capability compatible with the declared related-business contract.
Numeric workflows require a numeric child value_field.
decimal_summary additionally requires a required string group_field.
For nonnumeric workflows, unused value_field and group_field are null.
No unlisted workflow capability is inferred.

value_field.accepted: A child field with numeric type for numeric workflows; null when unused.
assertions: Reject a missing/non-child/non-numeric value field for numeric workflows.
Reject non-null value_field when not used.

group_field.accepted: Required string child field for decimal_summary; null when unused.
assertions: decimal_summary requires a required string group field.
Reject nullable/non-string/missing group field.
Reject non-null group_field when not used.
All declared types are accepted; unknown types are refused.
Inputs, step names, transaction names, branch names, and export names obey unique ASCII Python identifier rules, length <=64, no leading underscore or model_.
Input, step output, and literal reference forms remain distinct.
No forward refs; no refs across sibling branch arms; only branch exports become visible after the branch.
Both branch arms export the same names with matching types.
Equality/order comparisons require compatible scalar types; is_null requires nullable value and has no right operand.
Literal null is distinct from string 'null'; bool is distinct from integer; float -0.0 remains float and preserves sign.
Database writes occur in a transaction; transactions do not nest; no more than two transactions.
At most eight inputs and eight actions; at most two if nodes and branch depth two.
No delete action, source text, SQL, loops, parallel nodes, generated block IDs, or public bytes result.
Preserve ordered inputs/actions/branches/results; canonicalize object keys only where map semantics say so.
Typed scalar literal null is invalid for the supported literal types; null values enter through nullable references, never by coercing null to an omitted clause.
Flow object and array input records retain their exact typed schema; unknown fields and missing required fields are refused.
Repeated compile of identical canonical typed input and pinned catalog/contract hashes yields byte-identical complete bundle and files.
Compile chooses standard expected plan deterministically; it does not select alternate-standard vs alternate-checked variants by case ID.
Assemble accepts semantically valid alternate approved plans when every block and parameter is pinned and requested operations are covered.
Assemble rejects omitted requested operations and rejects reordered operations where the prompt contract requires order.

Both alternative-standard and alternative-checked original variants are checked by valid pinned-bundle assemble and archive byte parity; compile output is checked against standard expected semantics and bytes.
CNL-to-typed-prompt semantics match typed-JSON-to-bundle semantics for fields, routes, relation, capabilities, flow, and refusals.
